consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... she has astigmatism, which means her eyes don't focus properly on things. It's been a challenge for her, especially when trying to read or watch TV. We're really worried about how this might affect her learning.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She had fluid in her ear for a while, and we were so scared it would affect her hearing permanently. Luckily, after treatment, everything seems back to normal now. But I still get anxious whenever she complains about her ear.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing has been an issue for her since she started eating solid foods. Some foods are just too hard for her to manage. We've had to adjust her diet accordingly to make sure she can eat comfortably.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist says she needs regular check-ups to monitor her heart health. I try to stay on top of these appointments because I know how crucial they are for her well-being. It's always a relief when the results come back normal.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, she's been slower than her peers to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting. It was worrying at first, but with therapy and support, she's making progress. I'm just eager for her to catch up.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food textures can be a real issue for her. She's very picky and will only eat certain things if they're prepared in specific ways. Mealtime can be challenging, but we're learning to navigate her preferences.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... two main concerns. Firstly, her fontanelle took longer than usual to close completely. And secondly, her speech development isn't where it should be for her age. She doesn't speak as much as other children her age. Both these things worry me and I hope we can find ways to support her better.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart health check-ups to monitor her heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with food textures and has picky eating habits, limiting her meal options.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, is slower to reach certain milestones, and has speech development concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay, behavioral differences, or palatal abnormalities.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced fluid in the ear and has had issues with septal defects, which may impact her hearing and balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her vision and reading abilities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with tooth decay and sensitivity due to weak enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as cavities and gum disease can be common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed additional support in school, with some children requiring EHCP and others benefiting from mainstream education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support. 

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech development concerns and developmental delay, which are affecting her overall progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay, behavioral differences, and palatal abnormalities can be observed in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones and an increased curvature of the spine, which may affect his posture and movement.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and a proportion have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic cardiology check-ups.
b) Recommendations for treatments: N/A

This completes the required clinical patient report.

Parent: Her teeth seem prone to chipping or breaking easier than they should. Even minor accidents can cause noticeable damage‚ so we have to ensure she’s extra careful during meals and playtime to avoid any incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Compared to other kids‚ she tires out faster during physical activities. While she can run around and have fun‚ we notice she needs breaks sooner than her friends do. It might be related to her overall energy levels rather than a specific heart condition‚ but we keep an eye on it.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ she falls more frequently than other children her age. Whether it’s due to coordination or balance issues‚ we’re working with her to improve strength and agility to reduce these incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been challenging for her since infancy. Certain textures and tastes make mealtime difficult‚ and she has sensitivities to particular foods that trigger digestive discomfort.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned issues‚ our child moves slightly differently compared to her peers. There’s also a concern regarding delayed fontanelle closure‚ where certain bones in her skull took longer to fully close than typically expected. These aspects require periodic assessments to monitor progress and adjust care accordingly.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out faster than other kids during physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties since infancy, with sensitivities to particular foods triggering digestive discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more frequently than other children her age, indicating possible neurological or balance issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fluid buildup in her ears and has had issues with hearing clarity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasal grommet insertion to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects her vision and makes her struggle with focusing on distant objects.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth chipping or breaking, even with minor accidents, requiring careful handling during meals and playtime.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns are frequent, including weak enamel and need for regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out faster than her peers during physical activities, suggesting potential educational challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some children with KBG syndrome require additional support and some benefit from specialized settings, while others excel in mainstream settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and has feeding difficulties, leading to challenges in various areas of development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, those with KBG syndrome typically experience delays in reaching milestones such as rolling, sitting, walking, and using cutlery, zips, and buttons, but there is a wide range of eventual ability, with some acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and there are concerns regarding delayed fontanelle closure.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletally, some individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can cause complications like scoliosis and delayed fontanelle closure.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and palatal reviews if feeding difficulties or speech concerns are present.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring for tethered cord, considering surgical intervention if asymmetrical hip creases or painful gait are observed, ensuring proper nutrition and feeding management, and addressing any palatal abnormalities as they are identified.

This completes the required clinical patient report.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valvular abnormality in her heart that requires periodic monitoring to ensure everything remains stable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be picky with food and has experienced feeding difficulties, leading to stress at mealtimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences staring spells and lacks responsiveness during these episodes, suggesting potential neurological involvement.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media, a bacterial infection of the middle ear, which was treated with antibiotics.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and palatal abnormalities can lead to various ear infections and issues, requiring monitoring and treatment as needed.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of her eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, necessitating regular eye checks.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty chewing with tougher foods and requires regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues such as weak enamel and frequent tooth decay can be common, requiring careful brushing and possibly the need for early intervention.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has required additional support in school, indicating challenges with learning and behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help, with some benefiting from mainstream settings and others needing specialized support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient displays characteristics of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which impact her behavior and development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, while most children with KBG syndrome acquire mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children, there is a wide range of eventual ability, with some showing more obvious delay and others exhibiting fewer challenges.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletally, some individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can result in an increased curvature of the spine, and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and consideration for cardiac reviews following diagnosis.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve abnormality, treatment of otitis media, consideration for palatal review, and physical therapy to address neurological issues.

This completes the structured clinical patient report.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences a faster heartbeat than expected after physical activity, which is monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty eating certain food textures, avoiding specific foods based on their texture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences brief episodes of staring off into space, which are brief but noticeable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid buildup in the ear, which has led to conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced blurry vision and squint (astigmatism), where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as myopia (nearsightedness), hypermetropia (far-sightedness), and astigmatism.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental check-ups and visits due to tooth decay and need for fillings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular dental check-ups are essential to prevent further complications.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs additional support in school, requiring extra assistance to achieve academic goals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some individuals with KBG syndrome may need more support, while others excel in mainstream settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and has difficulty with certain tasks, such as playing with toys and using cutlery and zips.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit varying levels of delay, with some showing clear impairment and others displaying more normal development.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study showed that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and palatal reviews if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart conditions, treatment of tethered cord, correction of undescended testes, management of palatal abnormalities, and monitoring of skeletal anomalies.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty keeping up with peers during prolonged physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced issues with constipation and diarrhea, requiring adjustments to diet to regulate bowel movements.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epilepsy, requiring careful monitoring and adherence to prescribed medications to manage seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to squint when focusing, possibly indicating a connection between vision and ear health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear can worsen speech delay and impact hearing.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's eyes get tired easily, leading to frequent squinting and possible palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and requires regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and need for frequent dental interventions are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs additional support in school and may require accommodations to assist with learning and development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support, but overall there are varying levels of success and independence.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including squinting and palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which can impact their daily life and interactions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Various skeletal anomalies can be observed in individuals with KBG syndrome, including delayed fontanelle closure and hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic evaluations for palatal abnormalities.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and managing epilepsy, adjusting diet to regulate bowel movements, considering surgical intervention for palatal abnormalities and scoliosis, and ensuring proper nutrition to support overall health and development.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other children, particularly during physical activities or after short walks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, with challenges during meal times due to this issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and is being managed through physiotherapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have palatal abnormalities, which can affect speech development and feeding, requiring specialist review in some cases.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty making himself understood when trying to communicate, presenting as a feeding difficulty.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, with treatment and monitoring as per clinical guidelines.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups and has specific dental concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, with some children needing support in mainstream settings and others benefiting from specialized settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty making himself understood when trying to communicate, affecting his communication abilities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which may impact their development and daily life.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, which affects his mobility and posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Subtle anomalies of the palate can be present in some individuals with KBG syndrome, impacting speech development and feeding.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Management of hypotonia, consideration of tethered cord review and investigation based on clinical concerns, monitoring growth velocity, and provision of speech therapy and behavioral therapy as needed.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to get frustrated in noisy environments, suggesting potential otitis media or glue ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which affects his vision and ability to see distant objects clearly.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty during mealtimes and gets frustrated when eating, which affects her mood.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears less coordinated compared to peers, and simple tasks requiring balance and movement seem to challenge her more.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid in the ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had issues with otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as myopia and hypermetropia.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires more frequent dental check-ups and cleanings to prevent problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges during mealtimes and getting frustrated when eating, which affects her mood.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have varying levels of educational attainment, with some obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears less coordinated compared to peers and has challenges during mealtimes and getting frustrated when eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A small number of children with KBG syndrome have had hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's weight gain is slower compared to his peers, indicating potential issues with digestion or nutrient absorption.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally, which are distressing for him and the parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient turns the volume of the TV up very high to hear it clearly, suggesting he might be having some difficulty with his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has complained that things appear blurry to him, which can get frustrating during school lessons or when watching TV.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves differently and sometimes struggles with balance or running smoothly, indicating possible issues with coordination and movement.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome have subtler anomalies of the palate, which can affect speech development and feeding, and refernce for specialist review may be appropriate in some cases.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness more quickly than other kids his age, suggesting potential heart-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences irregular bowel movements, with some days being better than others and managing it primarily with diet changes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and constipation have been reported in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of staring off into space, which can last for a few seconds and indicate potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be managed with medication.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced glue ear in the past, and regular check-ups with specialists have helped mitigate the issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, or strabismus, which can affect his vision and lead to discomfort during activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and myopia, which may impact their daily life.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent cavities due to weak enamel and poor dental hygiene habits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues such as weak enamel and frequent cavities are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty expressing himself effectively and getting his ideas across, which impacts his academic performance and social interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often need additional support in school, with some benefiting from specialized settings and others adapting to mainstream environments.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and lacks clarity in communication, impacting his ability to interact effectively with peers and adults.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a hallmark of KBG syndrome, with varying levels of severity among affected individuals.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which may contribute to an increased curvature of the spine, and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various skeletal anomalies, including tethered cord, hip dysplasia, and palatal abnormalities.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic evaluations for heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and treating glaucoma, correcting hypotonia, providing physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as indicated by the patient's needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing when engaging in physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets much faster than expected when playing or running around, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems, getting constipated easily if she doesn't drink enough water or eat the right foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, affecting her muscle tone, and is being worked with physical therapists to improve.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media, an infection of the middle ear, which was treated with antibiotics.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which means she has difficulty seeing things clearly unless they're really close up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups to prevent further problems due to weak enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, indicating possible developmental delays and behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education levels vary among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some obtaining qualifications and others requiring more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and takes longer to reach milestones compared to peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with a wide range of eventual abilities.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can cause an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: N/A

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with eating a balanced diet due to being picky and having trouble chewing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and needs to manage seizures through medication adjustments and recognizing signs of impending seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media and glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss and affect her hearing and balance temporarily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and impact their overall hearing health.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities that affect her vision and balance, requiring periodic review and treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, which may be exacerbated by palatal abnormalities.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty with dental care due to poor tooth alignment and sensitivity to cold temperatures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges in school due to various factors including speech delay, feeding difficulties, and palatal abnormalities, which require support and accommodations.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some children staying in mainstream education and obtaining qualifications, while others may need more support and some benefit from specialized settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including palatal abnormalities and speech delay, which impact her overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a common feature in KBG syndrome, with a wide range of eventual abilities, from those with mild to those with more significant challenges.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, which affects her mobility and posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various skeletal anomalies, including asymmetric hip creases, asymmetric or painful gait, and tethered cord, which can impact their movement and posture.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and vision checks should be conducted to address potential issues.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart conditions, management of seizures, correction of palatal abnormalities, and orthopedic interventions as needed should be considered based on patient-specific findings.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things that are far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism (the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision), and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular visits to the dentist are essential to identify and address any potential issues.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional support in mainstream education and may require accommodations to assist with learning and development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support. The level of support required can differ greatly depending on the individual case.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and has difficulty catching up with peers in various areas, including motor skills, cognitive abilities, and social interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience challenges with speech delay, palatal abnormalities, and undescended testes, which can impact their communication and overall development.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study showed that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait. Additionally, some individuals may experience hip dysplasia, where the hip joints are easily dislocated.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and vision checks.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect, which is being monitored by a specialist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty eating and refusing to try new foods or non-favorite foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, characterized by stiffness in the muscles.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences problems with glue ear and discomfort when consuming cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as myopia, hypermetropia, and astigmatism.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and discomfort when consuming cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and need for frequent dental visits are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires additional support in school and may need occasional assistance with tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and has speech delay, as well as palatal abnormalities and hypotonia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to scoliosis and asymmetric hip creases.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic review for potential palatal abnormalities.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring for heart defects, addressing thyroid imbalances, managing seizures, treating sensorineural hearing loss, correcting undescended testes, and considering orthopedic interventions as needed.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing when engaging in physical activities, which is noticeable even when she's simply playing lightly indoors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing becomes much faster than expected for a child of her age and activity level when playing or running around, suggesting potential cardiac concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges during mealtimes, leaving food on her plate or showing little interest in eating certain dishes, leading to discussions about ensuring she gets enough nutrients.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences coordination issues, tripping over her own feet or having trouble catching a ball due to slower reactions compared to her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences discomfort and sensitivity to cold temperatures, particularly with cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes frequently when focusing on something, indicating possible visual strain.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, can occasionally be a feature in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity to cold stimuli, such as ice cream or cold water.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns may include weak enamel and various other factors that could lead to sensitivity or other issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges during mealtimes and experiences difficulties with coordination and balance, which may impact her educational performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some children with KBG syndrome may need additional support and some benefit from specialized settings, while others can thrive in mainstream environments with appropriate support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits coordination issues and struggles with slow reactions, which may affect her overall development and daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, most individuals with KBG syndrome experience delays in reaching milestones such as rolling, sitting, walking, and using cutlery, zips, and buttons, but there is a wide range of eventual ability, with some children acquiring these skills around the same age as "typical" children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Subtle anomalies of the palate, such as palatal abnormalities, can be present in some individuals with KBG syndrome, affecting speech development and feeding.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups, frequent monitoring of breathing rate during physical activities, and consideration for potential hormonal imbalances.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that requires monitoring by a cardiologist.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with mealtimes, including constipation or loose stools, which are managed through dietary adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a tethered cord, which is being monitored for potential developmental impacts.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced issues with fluid in the ear, leading to discomfort and hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which affects her ability to see clearly, requiring corrective measures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist regularly to prevent tooth decay and maintain overall oral health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular check-ups are essential to detect and address any issues promptly.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional support in school, including EHCP, to assist with academic and behavioral challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support. 

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits characteristics consistent with KBG syndrome, including developmental delays, behavioral differences, and speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which can impact their daily life.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which may lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and affect gait.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and palatal reviews if feeding difficulties or speech concerns are present.

Developmental delay is a common feature in KBG syndrome.
Some children with KBG syndrome acquire mobility and other skills around the same age as typical children.
Some children with KBG syndrome show more obvious delay.
Various skeletal anomalies can be present in individuals with KBG syndrome.
Individuals with KBG syndrome can have an increased curvature of the spine.
Individuals with KBG syndrome can have short fingers.
Individuals with KBG syndrome can have hip dysplasia.
Regular dental check-ups are recommended.
Hearing reviews at age 5 are recommended.
Palatal reviews are recommended if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
